item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / 42% of California voter names flagged by Trump admin not on rolls: Analysis

42% of California voter names flagged by Trump admin not on rolls: Analysis It's the first outside analysis of a list that the Department of Justice has used to threaten prosecution of election officials

The analysis also found that thousands of US citizens appear to be flagged as ineligible to vote on the government's list | Image Credit: Bloomberg

AP Washington 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 01 2026 | 7:43 AM IST

Listen to This Article

More than 4 in 10 names flagged as possible noncitizen voters in California by the Trump administration cannot even be found on the state's voter rolls, according to a legal filing Saturday by an immigrant rights group. It's the first outside analysis of a list that the Department of Justice has used to threaten prosecution of election officials. The analysis also found that thousands of US citizens appear to be flagged as ineligible to vote on the government's list. The contention was made in a filing by two UCLA data scientists who analysed the 20,930 names that the department demanded that California election officials treat as possible illegal voters by separating their ballots during the vote count on Election Day.

Multiple judges have rejected the demand as unconstitutional and a threat to democracy, and local and state officials have said the list appears riddled with errors. Also Read

US appeals court rejects Trump's bid to set aside 20,000 California votes

US judge orders removal of three Trump admin ads over political messaging

US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine, funded by allies

Trump says US in no hurry to end Iran war, claims time favours Washington

The breadth of its problems was outlined in Saturday's filing. It describes an analysis by two members of the UCLA's Voting Rights Project, who filed a lawsuit challenging it with the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights. The research found that 8,880 of the names, representing 42 per cent of the entire list, do not correspond to anyone on California's current voter file. It also found at least 22 are US citizens and many more may correspond to those of confirmed citizens.

"This review proves, at least as a preponderance of the evidence, that demands of election officials under criminal and civil threats, endangers the voting rights of plaintiff CHIRLA's members and clients," said the filing, which was co-signed by Xavier Becerra, the Democratic candidate for California governor and an adviser to the UCLA Voting Rights Project. The Trump administration had objected to sharing the list, calling it a "fishing expedition" and noting it included sensitive information.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.content:encoded: The French government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide Saturday in demonstrations focused on high living costs, fewer than in previous demonstrations.Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates. Organisers' turnout estimates are much higher.The Interior Ministry told reporters that of the 320,000 protesting Saturday, 70,000 people are estimated to have turned out for the main protest in Paris, which police moved outside the city centre to reduce the risk of unrest around government buildings and tourist sites after a last-minute court battle.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / US Secretary of State Rubio hosts Quad meet, wraps up G20 gathering

US Secretary of State Rubio hosts Quad meet, wraps up G20 gathering Rubio hosted a final plenary session with foreign ministers from the Group of 20 major economies during a two-day summit in Atlanta

In this image released on Oct. 31, 2026, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and other dignitaries during the G20 Ministerial Summit, in Atlanta, United States (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 31 2026 | 9:51 PM IST

US ??Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted a meeting with the foreign ministers of Australia, India and Japan on Saturday, their third meeting this year, as plans take shape for a summit of the leaders of the four countries in Manila next month.   The leaders' summit, expected to occur during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) conference in the Philippine capital on November 15-18, would be the first since 2024, and the first for US President Donald Trump.   The first formal leaders' summits of the four countries known as the Quad did not begin until President Joe Biden took office in 2021. Trump was scheduled to attend a Quad summit in India in late 2025, but canceled the visit due to trade frictions and tariff disputes with New Delhi.

After the Quad ministers' meeting, Rubio hosted a final plenary session with foreign ministers from the Group of 20 major economies during a two-day summit in Atlanta, where the participation of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov highlighted deep rifts among G20 members.   Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand told Reuters in an interview that she would not have chosen to invite Lavrov, but she used the occasion to confront him directly about Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.   Also Read

Military solutions not working, give diplomacy a chance: Jaishankar at G20

Jaishankar slams global energy disruptions through sanctions, chokepoints

Nvidia chief Jensen Huang reportedly targeted in Chinese spy plot

Refining the crude argument premium

Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes despite renewed US push for peace

"I stared him in the eye and called out Russia's further illegal invasion of Ukraine, the stealing of Ukrainian children, the targeting of Ukrainian ships in the Black Sea, all of which are reprehensible, all of which are contrary to international law and international humanitarian law," Anand said, citing her remarks during a closed-door plenary ??session on Friday.

Lavrov on Friday told reporters that Moscow's position on the Ukraine conflict was unchanged, and Russia could not accept Ukraine as a "military threat to the lawful security interests of the Russian Federation," according to Russian news agencies.   Rubio, speaking at a reception at the Georgia Aquarium on Friday evening, repeated his call for G20 members to cooperate where possible given today's complex economic and geopolitical challenges, including many with serious global consequences. "Because we all face these challenges, we must all work together to address them," he said.   "The future of our nations depends on our willingness to understand that while our interests may not always align, we should always seek to work together to advance them when and where they do align."

Rubio, who will hold a press conference after the meetings conclude on Saturday, said he hoped the G20 foreign ministers could lay the groundwork for a successful leaders' summit on December 14-15 at Trump's Doral golf resort near Miami.

item.title: Binance crypto exchange's $6.3 bn heist rattles crypto, draws scrutiny
item.description: The US agencies are coordinating with private-sector partners to assess the breach and recover stolen funds, while Binance pledged to cover all losses ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Myles Miller, Emily Nicolle and Scott Patterson US law enforcement joined the hunt for hackers who drained more than $6 billion from the Binance crypto exchange in the biggest cyber theft ever recorded. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is aware of the incident and is coordinating with its partners “to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps,” the agency said in a statement to Bloomberg News on Friday. Secret Service investigators are also “working around the clock” with the private sector to recover stolen funds, a spokesperson said. The Justice Department is aware of reports about the attack but does not comment on investigations, a spokesperson said.  While the full details of the Binance breach have yet to emerge, the incident comes amid growing concern about the risks posed by hackers in the age of artificial intelligence. Other recent cyberattacks have hit prediction market Polymarket, South Korean financial firms Mirae Asset Global Investments Co. and Daishin Securities, as well as Japanese currency trading platform GMO Internet Group Inc. The world’s largest crypto trading platform suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover all losses. The exchange is able to do so as a result of its ongoing investment of revenue into cryptocurrencies, Binance co-Chief Executive Officer Richard Teng said in a video posted on social media on Friday. Yi He, who is co-CEO, said Binance’s revenue for this year would completely cover the amount lost. Withdrawals were expected to resume by Sunday. “Most of what we earn from day-to-day operations is held in cryptoassets,” Teng said. “That is precisely why we are able to absorb a loss of this size, immediately, with our own money.”   Americans are prohibited from using the exchange. Binance.US is a smaller, separate entity.  The hack comes at a time when the Trump administration and its regulators have been pushing for mainstream adoption of cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology. In September, the Securities and Exchange Commission approved the so-called Innovation Exemption, which allows for public company stocks to trade on blockchains. The Binance hack is likely to raise concerns among public company executives about adopting such technology, experts said. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, for its part, recently unveiled a proposal to regulate digital asset transactions and markets. If finalized, the measure would regulate leveraged crypto trades offered to retail customers and establish a new category for crypto exchanges offering the leveraged trades to register with the agency. “There need to be delays and checkpoints” in transactions, said Austin Campbell, a crypto expert and former banker who is now an adjunct professor at the NYU Stern School of Business, drawing an analogy to automobile safety. “The car can be faster, cheaper and more gas efficient if we take out all the airbags and seatbelts,” he said.       Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs, Chainalysis and Elliptic have all pointed to North Korea as being behind the Binance heist, with Chainalysis labeling the incident as “the largest in the history of crypto, and one of the single-largest financial crimes of all time.” The funds drained in the attack were a mix of the largest cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, and the dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC. Bitcoin fell on news of the Binance attack, dropping below $77,000 for the first time in more than a month. The largest currency traded near the lows of the day for much of Friday.   For the crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident has cast a shadow over the recovery. Binance dwarfs its industry rivals. It holds roughly $135.2 billion in assets, compared with $28.6 billion at the second-largest exchange OKX, according to DefiLlama data.   Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop, as well as “additional points of breach.” It found no evidence of leaked private keys, it said. “This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance said in a post on X. An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve as a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around $1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024. The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze affected currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than $1.5 billion of the stablecoin USDT “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group Inc., said $800 million of its USDC token had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.”
